name: Reflective Stickers
seoTitle: Custom Reflective Stickers for Cars, Bikes and Safety Gear
seoDescription: Custom reflective stickers on engineer or high-intensity grade film that lights up in headlights. For vehicles, motorcycles, helmets and trailers. Free proof.
tagline: Printed on retroreflective vinyl that throws headlights straight back at the driver.
quickAnswer: Custom reflective stickers are printed on retroreflective vinyl, a film with glass beads or prisms that bounces light back toward its source, so a headlight or flashlight lights the sticker up at night. Fleet owners, motorcyclists, cyclists and safety managers use them on vehicles, trailers, helmets and equipment. Engineer or high-intensity grade, full-color print, from $0.30 per sticker, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Material: engineer or high-intensity reflective vinyl

sections.h2: Headlights hit it and it lights up: what reflective film actually does
sections.html:
Reflective vinyl does not glow and needs no charging. Its surface is packed with microscopic glass beads or prisms that send light back along the path it came from, so a driver whose headlights land on the sticker sees it flash bright while someone standing to the side sees an ordinary printed sticker. That is why road signs and the stripes on a trailer work at night. The sibling product, our glow in the dark sticker range, is the opposite mechanism: it stores light and emits a soft green glow in total darkness with no light source needed, which suits indoor exits and bedrooms, not traffic. Reflective is the one for anything a vehicle has to spot.

We print it for fleet door logos and DOT numbers, motorcycle and helmet decals, bike frame stripes, trailer and equipment markings, work-site hard hats, mailbox numbers and kids' backpacks and strollers.

sections.h2: Engineer grade or high-intensity: which reflective vinyl to order
sections.html:
Reflective films are sold by grade, which roughly means how far away a headlight picks them up and how long they last outside. We stock two for printed stickers.

GradeConstructionSeen fromOutdoor lifeOrder it for
Engineer gradeEnclosed glass beads, thin and flexibleRoughly 300 to 500 ft under low beamsAbout 5 yearsLogos, helmet and bike decals, mailbox numbers, promotional safety stickers
High-intensity gradeEncapsulated beads or microprisms, stiffer, brighterRoughly 1,000 ft and more7 to 10 yearsFleet markings, trailer stripes, equipment and site safety labels
Printed vs plainFull-color print over either gradePrinted areas reflect less than bare white filmAs the base filmKeep the brightest areas white or pale

Engineer grade bends around a helmet or a bike tube; high-intensity grade prefers flat or gently curved panels such as a truck door or a trailer side. If the sticker has to follow a compound curve, stay with engineer grade even if you want the extra brightness.

sections.h2: Where reflective stickers earn their place
sections.html:
• Cars and trucks: company logos and unit numbers on doors and tailgates, 6" to 12" wide, so a parked service van is visible on a dark street.
  • Motorcycles: tank, fender and pannier decals, plus thin stripes on the rear of the helmet where a following driver looks first.
  • Bicycles and e-bikes: 0.5" to 1" stripes on frame tubes, fork legs and crank arms; they catch headlights from every angle as the wheels turn.
  • Trailers, campers and equipment: conspicuity stripes and ID labels on the sides and rear, high-intensity grade for the longest reach.
  • Work sites: hard hat and tool box labels, cones and barriers, gate and hazard markings.
  • Home and school: house numbers on a mailbox, strollers, backpacks and wheelchairs used after dusk.

Other visibility materials, such as glow and fluorescent films, are grouped under the feature-based sticker categories if a job needs more than one.

sections.h2: Printing color on reflective vinyl: the trade-off nobody mentions
sections.html: Reflective film is at its brightest when it is bare, silver-white. Every layer of ink on top dims the return a little, and a solid dark block hardly reflects at all. So a full-color photo printed edge to edge on reflective vinyl looks great in daylight and does almost nothing at night. The fix is to design with the film in mind: leave the parts you want to flash as white or pale colors, reverse out the text so the letters are bare film inside a colored shape, and use the colored areas for daytime branding. Translucent reds, yellows and oranges reflect in their own color and are the standard choice for warning stripes. Pantone matches are possible in daylight, but check the night-time look on the proof, where we show the reflective areas separately. The full material list is on the Die Cut Stickers home page if you want a non-reflective version of the same design for indoor use.

1. Say where the sticker goes and how far away it needs to be seen. That decides engineer grade (curved, close range) or high-intensity (flat, long range).
  2. Send artwork as a vector file (AI, EPS, SVG or PDF) or a 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size, and mark which areas should stay bare film.
  3. Choose the shape: die cut to the outline, or a rectangle, circle or stripe. Sizes run from 0.5" up to 24" x 36".
  4. Pick permanent adhesive for vehicles and equipment, or removable for helmets and rental gear.
  5. Approve the free digital proof, which shows the print layer and the reflective layer, then allow 5 to 7 business days for production. FedEx shipping in the United States is free.

The minimum is 100 stickers, with prices from $0.30 per sticker depending on grade, size and quantity; fleets with several unit numbers can run them as one order with variable text.

sections.h2: Applying and keeping reflective decals bright
sections.html: Clean the panel with rubbing alcohol, apply dry, and work the squeegee from the center out; reflective film is stiffer than ordinary vinyl, so stretching it over a sharp curve cracks the bead layer and leaves a dark line. Apply above 50°F and give it 24 hours before a car wash. Hand wash is kinder than brushes, which scuff the laminate and dull the return over time. Road grime matters more than age: a dirty reflective sticker reflects far less, so wipe fleet markings down with the rest of the vehicle. For removal, warm with a heat gun on low and peel at a shallow angle; high-intensity grade comes off in larger pieces than engineer grade, which tends to flake.

faqs.q: How do custom reflective stickers work at night without a power source?
faqs.a: The film is loaded with tiny glass beads or prisms that send light back toward wherever it came from. When a headlight or flashlight hits the sticker, the light returns to the driver's eyes and the sticker appears to flash. Nothing is stored or emitted, so there is nothing to charge or replace.

faqs.q: Which reflective grade should I pick for reflective stickers on a car?
faqs.a: Engineer grade for logos and decals on doors, bumpers and curved panels; it is flexible, prints well and is visible from a few hundred feet. High-intensity grade for flat conspicuity markings on trucks and trailers where you want the longest reach and a 7 to 10 year life.

faqs.q: Can motorcycle reflective stickers bend around a helmet or tank?
faqs.a: Engineer grade can. It is thin enough to follow the curve of a helmet shell or a fuel tank if applied with gentle heat and no stretching. High-intensity grade is stiffer and will crack over a compound curve, so keep it for flat panniers, top boxes and trailer panels.

faqs.q: Will a full-color design printed on reflective vinyl still reflect?
faqs.a: The pale and white areas will; dark printed areas will not. Ink dims the return in proportion to how dark it is. Design with bare or light film where you want the flash, use reversed-out text, and keep solid dark blocks small. We show the reflective areas on the proof.

faqs.q: How long do reflective stickers last on a truck or trailer outdoors?
faqs.a: Engineer grade holds its brightness for about 5 years outside, high-intensity grade for 7 to 10 years, both with the laminate we apply as standard. Keeping them clean matters as much as the grade, because a layer of road film can cut the reflection by half.

faqs.q: Can I order reflective stickers with different unit numbers for a fleet?
faqs.a: Yes. Send a list of unit, DOT or asset numbers and we print each sticker with its own number on the same run. The minimum is 100 stickers in total, not per number, so a fleet of 20 vehicles with five stickers each hits it in one order.

faqs.q: Are reflective stickers legal to put on a car or bicycle?
faqs.a: On the body, bumpers, helmets and bike frames, yes, in every state we know of. Rules apply to colors near lights: avoid red on the front and white on the rear of a vehicle, and keep stickers off headlamps, tail lamps and license plates. Check your state's code for trailers.

faqs.q: Does reflective film come in colors other than silver?
faqs.a: Yes. Translucent red, yellow and orange reflective films reflect in their own color and are standard for warning stripes and hazard labels. Any other color is printed on silver-white film, where pale colors keep most of the reflection and dark colors lose it.

faqs.q: Can reflective decals be removed from a vehicle without damaging the paint?
faqs.a: Yes, on factory paint. Warm the decal with a heat gun on low, lift a corner and peel at a shallow angle, then clean any adhesive trace with rubbing alcohol. Removable adhesive makes this easier on helmets and rental gear; permanent adhesive on a truck takes more patience but comes off.

faqs.q: What size reflective sticker is visible from a reasonable distance at night?
faqs.a: For a driver to read text, plan on 1" of letter height per 100 ft on high-intensity film and a little more on engineer grade. A 6" x 12" door logo is visible as a bright shape from well over 500 ft; 0.5" bike stripes show as moving flashes from a block away.

faqs.q: Do reflective stickers survive car washes and pressure washing?
faqs.a: Hand washes and touchless automatic washes, yes. Brush washes scuff the laminate over time and dull the reflection, and a pressure washer aimed at the edge from close range will lift any sticker. Wait 24 hours after application before the first wash.

faqs.q: How many custom reflective stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 stickers, which can be split across shapes and numbers on one order. Prices start at $0.30 per sticker and depend on grade, size and quantity, with high-intensity film costing more than engineer grade. Production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the free proof.
